question: Who coined the term ‘zeroth law of thermodynamics’ in 1931, which asserts that two bodies in equilibrium with a third are in equilibrium with each other?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ralph H Fowler**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Zeroth law of thermodynamics is one of the four laws of thermodynamics.
 
• Its creation is credited to Ralph H. Fowler.
 
• The Zeroth law of thermodynamics frames the concept of temperature as an indicator of thermal equilibrium.
 
• According to the Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics, "two systems in thermal equilibrium with a third system separately are in thermal equilibrium with each other."
 
• The Zeroth Law plainly states that when two systems A and B are in thermal equilibrium, there must be a physical quantity that has the same value for both.
 
• Temperature is a thermodynamic variable whose value is the same for two systems in thermal equilibrium (T ).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The first law of thermodynamics states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only altered in form.
 
• The total entropy of an isolated system (the thermal energy per unit temperature that is unavailable for doing productive work) can never decrease, according to the second law of thermodynamics.
 
• When a current 'i' travels through a conductor of resistance 'r' for time 't,' Joule's law of heating states that the heat created in the conductor is equal to the product of the square of the current, the resistance, and the duration.
